newsitem.title: GREECE: IRAQI ENVOY TO GREECE SLAMS TURKISH INCURSION.
newsitem.headline: IRAQI ENVOY TO GREECE SLAMS TURKISH INCURSION.

text.p: Baghdad's ambassador to Athens on Wednesday slammed Turkey's incursion into Iraq as a violation of international law and warned his country had the right to answer "accordingly", the semi-official Athens News Agency said.

"Turkey's action constitutes a blatant violation of Iraq's sovereignty and integrity was well as international agreements, laws and the principles of good neighbourliness," ambassador Issam Khalil was quoted as saying.
The agency said Khalil warned Ankara, which has fought Kurdish revels in northern Iraq for eight days, that Baghdad was entitled to "reply accordingly to Turkey's aggressive act".
"Turkey must stop acting like a phoney policeman and realise that the era of aging and sick empires is gone forever," the envoy was quoted as saying.
More than 10,000 Turkish troops last week began a major cross-border operation in pursuit of PKK separatists who use northern Iraq as a base to launch raids into southeast Turkey.

Turkey showed no signs of letting up on the operation on Wednesday, ferrying in more troops and supplies, ignoring criticism from its Western allies, the United Nations as well as countries in the region.
Military sources say more than 1,300 PKK rebels have been killed so far but PKK sources say that figure is grossly inflated.
